page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1.4xlarge is a storage-oriented virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. Powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 CPU operating at 2.5 GHz, the instance features 16 dedicated vCPUs on the x86_64 architecture paired with 64.0 GB of RAM, yielding a ratio of 4.0 GB of memory per core. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps.

The distinguishing hardware characteristic of the ecs.d1.4xlarge is its integrated local storage configuration, providing 47,244 GB of hard disk drive (HDD) capacity directly attached to the virtual machine. This extremely high capacity per node yields substantial cost efficiency for sequential read/write operations and high-volume data retention compared to network-attached block volumes. However, reliance on magnetic spinning disks presents an architectural tradeoff, favoring total storage volume and bulk throughput over the low-latency random IOPS offered by solid-state hardware.

Given its dense HDD provision and 16 dedicated core count, the server is structured for big data processing, distributed file systems, continuous log collection, data warehousing, and batch processing pipelines where massive local storage capacity is required without requiring high IOPS or dedicated GPU acceleration.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1.4xlarge is a high-density storage instance running on the KVM hypervisor and powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor operating at 2.5 GHz. Configured with 16 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs and 64.0 GB of RAM, it maintains a standard 4.0 GB per vCPU memory balance accompanied by a 6 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The primary hardware highlight is its bundled 47,244 GB local HDD storage capacity, delivering high local disk volume for bulk data management. While magnetic HDD storage trade off low-latency random access IOPS for physical capacity density, this configuration provides notable cost efficiency for large-scale sequential data operations without incurring external storage overhead. The absence of GPU accelerators and advanced vector instruction flags keeps the focus strictly on general compute and high-capacity local storage tasks. The instance fits heavy log analytics, big data processing, distributed file storage, and data warehousing workloads.
